title: Relative etale scheme atlases for Deligne--Mumford fibre products
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Stacks, Deligne--Mumford stacks, algebraic spaces and 2-fibre products have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Representable by algebraic spaces means that every scheme base change is equivalent to an algebraic space. Properties of such maps are tested on these algebraic-space base changes. An etale scheme chart is a representable-by-algebraic-spaces etale morphism from a scheme; an atlas is a surjective chart. Etale uses [def-weil-etale-morphism] on scheme charts. Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y,\mathcal Z$ be Deligne--Mumford stacks over $S$ and let $\mathcal X\to\mathcal Z$, $\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ be morphisms. The stack $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal Y$ is Deligne--Mumford and has an etale scheme atlas. Representable-by-algebraic-spaces etale maps between these stacks are preserved by base change and composition; if the given maps are surjective then their base changes and compositions are surjective. In any 2-commutative diagram $U\to V$ above $\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$, with etale scheme charts $U\to\mathcal X$ and $V\to\mathcal Y$, the induced map $U\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ is etale, without any surjectivity assumption on the charts.

proof.text:
Put $\mathcal P=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal Y$. In the triple description of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], descent data for $(x,y,\alpha)$ consist of descent data for $x,y$ and compatible local arrows $\alpha:f(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}g(y)$. Descend $x,y$ using their stack conditions; the sheaf condition for isomorphisms in $\mathcal Z$ glues the local $\alpha$ uniquely. The same argument glues arrows, so $\mathcal P$ is a stack. For two triples $a=(x,y,\alpha)$ and $a'=(x',y',\alpha')$ over a scheme $T$, their isomorphism sheaf is
$$\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X}(x,x')\times_{\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Z}(f(x),g(y'))}\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Y}(y,y'),$$
where the two maps send $u$ to $\alpha'f(u)$ and $v$ to $g(v)\alpha$. This follows exactly from the arrow equation in the triple definition. All three Isom sheaves are algebraic spaces by [lem-sfb-dm-isom-space-unramified]; their fibre product is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For a scheme test $T\to\mathcal P\times_S\mathcal P$ corresponding to $(a,a')$, an object of the diagonal base change is a triple $c$ together with arrows $i:c\xrightarrow{\sim}a$ and $j:c\xrightarrow{\sim}a'$. Send it to $ji^{-1}$. Conversely an arrow $k:a\xrightarrow{\sim}a'$ gives $(a,\mathrm{id},k)$; every original triple is uniquely isomorphic to this one by $i$. These assignments commute with restriction, identifying the diagonal base change with the displayed Isom sheaf. Hence the diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces.

proof.text: Choose etale scheme atlases $U\to\mathcal X$ and $V\to\mathcal Y$, as supplied by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], and form the scheme $T_0=U\times_SV$ using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Pulling the two chart objects to $T_0$ and mapping them into $\mathcal Z$ gives objects $z_U,z_V$. By [lem-sfb-dm-isom-space-unramified], $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Z/T_0}(z_U,z_V)$ is an algebraic space $R$. A map $T\to R$ is precisely a pair $T\to U,T\to V$ and an isomorphism between their images in $\mathcal Z(T)$. Thus $R$ represents $U\times_{\mathcal Z}V$ and has a natural map $r:R\to\mathcal P$. Explicitly the inverse sends a triple $(u,v,\alpha)$ over $T$ to the section of the pulled-back Isom sheaf represented by $\alpha$. Since $U,V$ are schemes viewed as discrete groupoids, an arrow of triples fixes $u,v$ and exists exactly when the two $\alpha$ agree; it is then unique. These assignments are inverse and commute with arbitrary restrictions in $T$. No scheme representability of $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 04TF (lemma-2-fibre-product-general), atlas construction; Tag 045G (lemma-representable-diagonal), conditions (2) and (4).

proof.text:
For every scheme $T\to\mathcal P$ with triple $(x,y,\alpha)$, put $B=U\times_{\mathcal X}T$ and $C=V\times_{\mathcal Y}T$. Since the chosen maps are atlases, $B,C$ are algebraic spaces etale and surjective over $T$. The triple description gives $R\times_{\mathcal P}T\simeq B\times_TC$: the two chosen lifts and their isomorphisms to $x,y$ force the compatibility isomorphism to be their composite with $\alpha$. The fibre product is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and its projection to $T$ is etale and surjective by base change and composition in [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Hence $r$ is representable by algebraic spaces, etale and surjective. Choose an etale scheme atlas $W\to R$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. After every scheme test $T\to\mathcal P$, its base change is the composite
$$W\times_R(B\times_TC)\longrightarrow B\times_TC\longrightarrow T.$$
The same algebraic-space permanence theorem makes both arrows etale and surjective. Thus $W\to\mathcal P$ is an etale surjective scheme atlas. Together with step 1 this proves that $\mathcal P$ is Deligne--Mumford.

proof.text: For the remaining permanence assertions we may use the algebraic-stack formulation. The etale scheme atlases of a Deligne--Mumford stack are smooth on scheme charts by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. The representable diagonal and smooth surjective atlas therefore satisfy [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent], giving an fppf algebraic stack with unchanged diagonal and atlas. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] to the representable-by-algebraic-spaces etale maps: it gives arbitrary base-change and composition stability. Its current statement also identifies field-extension local lifting with the surjectivity chart test: for every scheme $T\to\mathcal Y$ and every surjective etale scheme chart $A\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T$, the scheme map $A\to T$ is surjective. Thus the surjectivity hypothesis in our chart convention gives field-extension lifting; the cited permanence preserves it, and the same equivalence recovers chart-test surjectivity for the resulting representable maps. The theorem applies to both the original stacks and the fibre products constructed in steps 1--3.

proof.text:
For the final clause let $E=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}V$ and let $h:U\to E$ be the map defined by the given 2-commutative square. The scheme $V$ is itself a Deligne--Mumford stack: by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space] $h_V$ is an fppf, hence etale, sheaf, so as a discrete fibred groupoid it is a stack; for $a,b\in h_V(T)$ the sheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_T(a,b)$ is the equalizer $h_T\times_{h_V\times_Sh_V}h_V$, a scheme by that node's diagonal clause, and the identity of $h_V$ is a surjective etale scheme atlas. Hence steps 1--3, applied to $\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\leftarrow V$, show that $E$ is Deligne--Mumford; step 4 makes $q:E\to\mathcal X$ representable etale, since it is a base change of $V\to\mathcal Y$. For any scheme $t:T\to E$, the spaces
$$B=U\times_{\mathcal X}T,\qquad D=E\times_{\mathcal X}T$$
are etale over $T$: their maps to $T$ are base changes of $U\to\mathcal X$ and $q$. The map $h$ induces a map $B\to D$ over $T$, sending $(u,t,\beta)$ to $(h(u),t,\beta)$; the stipulated 2-isomorphism identifies $qh$ with the chart map $U\to\mathcal X$. Since both spaces are etale over $T$, this induced map is etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. The map $t$ gives the section $s:T\to D$, $t_0\mapsto(t(t_0),t_0,\mathrm{id})$. Explicitly, a $T$-scheme $T_1$ maps to $B\times_{D,s}T$ by a lift $u:T_1\to U$, an isomorphism $\beta:qh(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}qt|_{T_1}$, and an arrow $\gamma:h(u)\xrightarrow{\sim}t|_{T_1}$ whose image under $q$ is $\beta$. This is precisely the triple giving a map to $U\times_ET$: forgetting $\beta$ and recovering it as $q(\gamma)$ are inverse on objects and arrows and commute with restriction in $T_1$. This fibre product is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and its projection to $T$ is etale by base change of $B\to D$. Thus every scheme base change of $h$ is algebraic-space etale, proving the assertion. Neither chart was assumed surjective.
